title: Pool Allocators
summary: A pool hands out blocks of one fixed size from a single region. Free blocks are linked into a list through their own memory, so allocating and freeing are a couple of pointer moves, with no headers and no fragmentation. Building one, and where games use them.

cards.q: Why does a pool allocator have no fragmentation?
cards.a: Every block is the same size, so any free block satisfies any request.

cards.q: Where does the pool keep the list of free blocks?
cards.a: As a linked list whose next pointers are stored in the first bytes of the free blocks themselves.

cards.q: Why must each block be at least sizeof(void*) bytes?
cards.a: A free block has to hold the pointer to the next free block.

cards.q: Why do use-after-free bugs on pooled objects show up quickly?
cards.a: The freed block's first bytes are overwritten by the free-list pointer at once, and the block is the next one handed out.
